value.zh: 嗣昭危甚，問圜去就之計，圜勸嗣昭堅守以待，不可有二心。
value.en: Sizhao was desperate and asked Huan whether to stay or go. Huan urged him to hold on and wait and never waver.
value.literal: Sizhao was in grave peril and asked Huan whether to stay or leave. Huan urged Sizhao to hold firm and wait—he must not waver.

value.zh: 已而莊宗攻破梁夾城，聞圜為嗣昭畫守計，甚嘉之，由是益知名。
value.en: Zhuangzong soon broke the Liang encircled fort. Learning Huan had planned Sizhao’s defense, he praised him warmly, and Huan’s name spread.
value.literal: Before long Zhuangzong broke the Liang encircled fort. Hearing that Huan had devised Sizhao’s defense plan, he greatly praised him, and from then on Huan grew more famous.

value.zh: 其後嗣昭與莊宗有隙，圜數奉使往來，辨釋讒構，嗣昭卒免於禍，圜之力也。
value.en: Later Sizhao and Zhuangzong quarreled. Huan shuttled between them, clearing away slander, and Sizhao at last escaped ruin—Huan’s work.
value.literal: Later Sizhao and Zhuangzong fell out. Huan repeatedly went back and forth as envoy, explaining away slanders and intrigues, and Sizhao at last escaped disaster—this was Huan’s doing.

value.zh: 嗣昭從莊宗戰胡柳，擊敗梁兵，圜頗有功，莊宗勞之曰：「儒士亦破體邪？
value.en: Sizhao followed Zhuangzong to Huliu and routed the Liang army. Huan served well. Zhuangzong praised him: “Even a scholar casts off restraint?
value.literal: Sizhao followed Zhuangzong to fight at Huliu and routed the Liang army. Huan did considerable service. Zhuangzong praised him: “A scholar too throws off restraint?

value.zh: 仁者之勇，何其壯也！」
value.en: The courage of the humane—how mighty!”
value.literal: The courage of the humane—how mighty!”

value.zh: 王镕，其先回鶻阿布思之遺種，曰沒諾幹，為鎮州王武俊騎將，武俊錄以為子，遂冒姓王氏。
value.en: Wang Rong traced his line to Mo Nuogan, a survivor of the Uyghur chief Abu Si. Mo Nuogan served Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou as a mounted officer; Wujun adopted him, and the family took the name Wang.
value.literal: Wang Rong: his ancestors were descendants of the Uyghur Abu Si, named Mo Nuogan, a cavalry officer of Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou; Wujun adopted him as a son, and he took the surname Wang.

value.zh: 沒諾幹子曰末垣活，末垣活子曰升，升子曰廷湊，廷湊子曰元達，元達子曰紹鼎、紹懿，紹鼎子曰景崇。
value.en: Mo Nuogan begat Mo Yuanhuo, who begat Sheng, then Tingcou, then Yuanda. Yuanda had Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding begat Jingchong.
value.literal: Mo Nuogan’s son was Mo Yuanhuo; Mo Yuanhuo’s son was Sheng; Sheng’s son was Tingcou; Tingcou’s son was Yuanda; Yuanda’s sons were Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding’s son was Jingchong.

value.zh: 自升以上三世，常為鎮州騎將，自景崇以上四世五人，皆為成德軍節度使。
value.en: For three generations before Sheng the family held cavalry commands at Zhenzhou; for four generations from Jingchong, five men in succession ruled Chengde.
value.literal: From Sheng upward for three generations they were constantly Zhenzhou cavalry officers; from Jingchong upward for four generations five men all were military commissioners of the Chengde army.

value.zh: 景崇官至守太尉，封常山郡王，唐中和二年卒。
value.en: Jingchong rose to Acting Grand Marshal and Prince of Changshan; he died in Zhonghe 2 of Tang.
value.literal: Jingchong reached the office of Acting Grand Marshal, was enfeoffed Prince of Changshan, and died in the second year of Tang Zhonghe.

value.zh: 子鎔立，年十歲。
value.en: His son Rong succeeded him at the age of ten.
value.literal: His son Rong succeeded, ten years old.

value.zh: 是時，晉新有太原，李匡威據幽州，王處存據中山，赫連鐸據大同，孟方立據邢臺，四面豪傑並起而交爭。
value.en: Jin had just secured Taiyuan. Li Kuangwei held Youzhou, Wang Chucun Zhongshan, Helian Duo Datong, Meng Fangli Xingtai—warlords sprang up on all sides and tore at one another.
value.literal: At that time Jin had newly taken Taiyuan; Li Kuangwei held Youzhou, Wang Chucun held Zhongshan, Helian Duo held Datong, and Meng Fangli held Xingtai—heroes rose on every side and fought one another.

value.zh: 镕介於其間，而承祖父百年之業，士馬強而畜積富，為唐累世藩臣。
value.en: Rong sat in the middle of them all, heir to a century of Wang power: strong cavalry, deep granaries, a Tang vassal line for generations.
value.literal: Rong stood between them, yet inherited his grandfather’s enterprise of a hundred years: strong soldiers and horses, rich stores—a Tang frontier house for generations.

value.zh: 故镕年雖少，藉其世家以取重，四方諸鎮廢立承繼，有請於唐者，皆因镕以聞。
value.en: Young as he was, the Wang name gave him weight. Whenever a circuit asked the court to confirm a change of ruler, the word passed through Rong.
value.literal: Thus though Rong was young, he drew weight from his house; when the circuits sought Tang’s approval for deposition, succession, or appointment, the petition always went through Rong.

value.zh: 初，匡威悅其弟匡儔之婦美而淫之，匡儔怒，及其救镕也，誘其軍亂而自立。
value.en: Li Kuangwei had taken his brother Kuangchou’s wife and seduced her; Kuangchou burned with anger. When he marched to save Rong he turned the troops against his brother and seized Youzhou for himself.
value.literal: Earlier Kuangwei had coveted his brother Kuangchou’s wife for her beauty and lain with her; Kuangchou was enraged. When he came to rescue Rong he incited the army to mutiny and set himself up as ruler.

value.zh: 匡威內慚不敢還，乃以符印歸其弟，而將奔於京師。
value.en: Too ashamed to face his men, Kuangwei handed the seals to Kuangchou and set out for the capital.
value.literal: Ashamed within, Kuangwei dared not return; he returned the seals to his brother and prepared to flee to the capital.

value.zh: 行至深州，镕德匡威救己，使人邀之，館於梅子園，以父事之。
value.en: At Shenzhou, Rong—mindful that Kuangwei had saved him—sent for him and housed him at Meizi Garden, honoring him like a parent.
value.literal: When he reached Shenzhou, Rong, grateful that Kuangwei had saved him, sent men to invite him and lodged him at Meizi Garden, treating him as a father.

value.zh: 匡威客李正抱者，少遊燕、趙間，每徘徊常山，愛之不能去。
value.en: One of Kuangwei’s companions was Li Zhengbao. As a young man he had wandered Yan and Zhao; each time he passed Changshan he lingered, unable to tear himself away.
value.literal: Among Kuangwei’s followers was Li Zhengbao, who in youth had roamed Yan and Zhao and, lingering at Changshan, loved the place and could not leave.

value.zh: 正抱、匡威皆失國無聊，相與登城西高閣，顧覽山川，泫然而泣，乃與匡威謀劫而代之。
value.en: Zhengbao and Kuangwei, both landless and idle, climbed the western tower, gazed over the landscape until they wept, and hatched a plan to seize Rong by force.
value.literal: Zhengbao and Kuangwei, both exiles with nothing to do, climbed the high pavilion west of the city, looked over the hills and rivers, wept, and plotted to seize Rong’s place.

value.zh: 因詐為忌日，镕去衛從，晨詣館慰，坐定，甲士自幕後出，持镕兩袖，镕曰：「吾國賴公而存，誠無以報厚德，今日之事，是所甘心。」
value.en: They staged a memorial day. Rong came at dawn without escort to comfort Kuangwei at the lodge. As he sat down, soldiers in armor rushed from behind the screen and gripped his sleeves. Rong said: “You preserved our house—I could never repay you. Do as you will; I submit.”
value.literal: They feigned a day of mourning; Rong left his guards and came at dawn to the lodge to offer condolences. Once seated, armored men burst from behind the curtain and seized both his sleeves. Rong said: “Our state survived only through you—I have no way to repay such kindness. What you do today I accept willingly.”

value.zh: 因叩頭以位與匡威。
value.en: He kowtowed and offered Kuangwei the command.
value.literal: He then kowtowed and yielded the throne to Kuangwei.

value.zh: 匡威素少镕，以謂無能為也，因與镕方轡詣府，將代其位。
value.en: Kuangwei had always despised the boy and thought him harmless. He rode beside Rong to the yamen, ready to replace him.
value.literal: Kuangwei had always looked down on the young Rong and thought him incapable; he rode side by side with Rong to the headquarters, about to take his place.

value.zh: 行過親事營，軍士閉門大噪，天雨震電，暴風拔木，屋瓦皆飛。
value.en: Passing the household guard camp, the troops slammed the gates and roared. Rain poured, lightning split the sky, wind tore up trees, and tiles flew from the roofs.
value.literal: As they passed the personal-guard camp the soldiers shut the gates and raised a great clamor; rain fell, thunder rolled, a gale uprooted trees, and roof tiles flew through the air.

value.zh: 屠者墨君和望見镕，識之，從缺垣中躍出，挾镕於馬，負之而走，亂軍擊殺匡威、正抱，燕人皆走。
value.en: Mo Junhe the butcher spotted Rong, knew him, scrambled through a broken wall, hauled him onto a horse, and fled. The rebels killed Kuangwei and Zhengbao; every man from Yan ran.
value.literal: The butcher Mo Junhe saw Rong, recognized him, leaped through a gap in the wall, seized him onto a horse, and carried him away; the mutineers killed Kuangwei and Zhengbao, and all the Yan men fled.

value.zh: 匡儔雖憾其兄，而陽以大義責镕甚急。
value.en: Kuangchou hated his brother, yet in public he rebuked Rong in the name of justice.
value.literal: Though Kuangchou resented his brother, outwardly he pressed Rong hard with righteous blame.

value.zh: 镕既失燕援，而晉軍急攻平山，劫镕以盟，镕遂與晉和。
value.en: Cut off from Yan, Rong faced a fierce Jin attack on Pingshan. Jin held him to ransom for peace, and he submitted.
value.literal: Rong, having lost Yan’s support, faced Jin’s urgent assault on Pingshan; Jin took him hostage to force an alliance, and Rong made peace with Jin.

value.zh: 其後梁太祖下晉邢、洺、磁三州，乃為書詔镕，使絕晉而歸梁，镕依違不決。
value.en: When Liang Taizu seized Xing, Ming, and Ci from Jin he wrote Rong demanding he abandon Jin for Liang. Rong hesitated.
value.literal: Later Liang Taizu took Jin’s Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures and sent an edict ordering Rong to break with Jin and return to Liang; Rong wavered, unable to decide.

value.zh: 晉將李嗣昭復取洺州，梁太祖擊敗嗣昭，嗣昭棄洺州走。
value.en: Li Sizhao of Jin retook Mingzhou. Liang Taizu routed him, and Sizhao abandoned the city and fled.
value.literal: Jin’s general Li Sizhao retook Mingzhou; Liang Taizu defeated Sizhao, and Sizhao abandoned Mingzhou and fled.

value.zh: 梁獲其輜重，得镕與嗣昭書，多道梁事，太祖怒，因移兵常山，顧謂葛從周曰：「得鎮州以與爾，爾為我先鋒。」
value.en: Liang took the supply train and found Rong’s letters to Sizhao, full of talk about Liang. Taizu flew into a rage, marched on Changshan, and told Ge Congzhou: “Zhenzhou is yours—lead the van.”
value.literal: Liang captured the baggage train and found letters between Rong and Sizhao that spoke often of Liang’s affairs; the Taizu was furious, shifted his army to Changshan, and said to Ge Congzhou: “I give you Zhenzhou—be my vanguard.”

value.zh: 從周至臨城，中流矢，臥輿中，梁軍大沮。
value.en: At Lincheng Congzhou took an arrow and had to be carried in a litter; Liang’s army lost heart.
value.literal: Congzhou reached Lincheng, took an arrow in the stream, and lay in a litter; the Liang army was greatly discouraged.

value.zh: 梁太祖自將傅城下，焚其南關，镕懼，顧其屬曰：「事急矣！
value.en: Taizu himself pressed the siege and fired the south gate. Rong, terrified, turned to his officers: “This is the end!
value.literal: Liang Taizu personally led the assault below the walls and burned the south gate. Rong was afraid and said to his men: “Matters are desperate!

value.zh: 奈何？」
value.en: What can we do?"
value.literal: What can we do?”

value.zh: 判官周式，辨士也，對曰：「此難與力爭，而可以理奪也。」
value.en: Zhou Shi, a gifted speaker, answered: “You cannot beat them in battle. You may yet move them with argument.”
value.literal: His staff officer Zhou Shi, a man of eloquence, replied: “This is not a fight to win by force—but it can be won by reason.”

value.zh: 式與梁太祖有舊，因請入梁軍。
value.en: Shi was an old acquaintance of Taizu’s and asked leave to go to the Liang lines.
value.literal: Shi had old ties with Liang Taizu and asked to enter the Liang camp.

value.zh: 太祖望見式，罵曰：「吾常以書招镕不來，今吾至此，而爾為說客，晚矣！
value.en: Taizu spotted him and raged: “I wrote Rong again and again—he ignored me. Now I am at his gates and you come as a go-between? It is too late!
value.literal: Taizu saw him from afar and cursed: “I wrote again and again summoning Rong—he would not come. Now that I am here you play the envoy? Too late!

value.zh: 且晉吾仇也，而镕附之，吾知李嗣昭在城中，可使先出。」
value.en: Jin is my enemy, and Rong sides with them. I know Sizhao is inside—send him out first."
value.literal: And Jin is my enemy, yet Rong clings to them. I know Li Sizhao is in the city—have him come out first."

value.zh: 乃以所得镕與嗣昭書示式，式進曰：「梁欲取一鎮州而止乎，而欲成霸業於天下也？
value.en: He flung the letters before Shi. Shi stepped forward: “Does Liang want one prefecture—or the realm?
value.literal: He then showed Shi the captured letters. Shi advanced and said: “Does Liang mean to take only one Zhenzhou—or to win empire under Heaven?

value.zh: 且霸者責人以義而不私，今天子在上，諸侯守封睦鄰，所以息爭，且休民也。
value.en: A true conqueror judges by duty, not spite. The Son of Heaven still reigns; the circuits hold their borders and live as neighbors—that is how wars end and the people breathe.
value.literal: A hegemon holds men to righteousness, not to private gain. Today the Son of Heaven sits above; the feudatories guard their fiefs and keep peace with their neighbors—that is how strife ends and the people rest.

value.zh: 昔曹公破袁紹，得魏將吏與紹書，悉焚之，此英雄之事乎！
value.en: When Cao Cao crushed Yuan Shao he found his officers’ letters to the enemy and burned them—is that not how a great man acts?
value.literal: When Duke Cao broke Yuan Shao he found letters between Shao and his own officers and burned them all—is that not the act of a hero?

value.zh: 今梁知兵舉無名，而假嗣昭以為辭。
value.en: Liang knows this war has no just cause and hides behind Sizhao’s name.
value.literal: Now Liang knows this campaign has no good name and uses Sizhao only as a pretext.

value.zh: 且王氏五世六公撫有此士，豈無死士，而待嗣昭乎？」
value.en: Five generations of Wangs have ruled this soil—do you imagine they have no loyal dead, and that only Sizhao stands between you and them?”
value.literal: The Wang house for five generations and six lords has held this land—do you think they have no men who would die for them, waiting on Sizhao?”

value.zh: 太祖大喜，起牽式衣而撫之曰：「吾言戲耳。」
value.en: Taizu laughed with delight, rose, took Shi by the sleeve, and said: “I was only testing you.”
value.literal: The Taizu was greatly pleased, rose, took Shi by the robe, and stroked him, saying: “My words were in jest.”

value.zh: 因延式於上坐，議與镕和。
value.en: He gave Shi the seat of honor and opened talks for peace with Rong.
value.literal: He seated Shi in the place of honor and discussed peace with Rong.

value.zh: 镕以子昭祚為質，梁太祖以女妻之。
value.en: Rong sent his son Zhaozuo as hostage; Taizu married him to a Liang princess.
value.literal: Rong sent his son Zhaozuo as hostage; Liang Taizu gave him his daughter in marriage.

value.zh: 太祖即位，封镕趙王。
value.en: When Taizu became emperor he made Rong Prince of Zhao.
value.literal: When the Taizu took the throne he enfeoffed Rong Prince of Zhao.

value.zh: 镕祖母喪，諸鎮皆吊，梁使者見晉使在館，還言趙王有二誌。
value.en: At his grandmother’s funeral every circuit sent mourners. A Liang envoy saw Jin’s envoy at the same guesthouse and reported that the Zhao prince was playing both sides.
value.literal: When Rong’s grandmother died every circuit sent condolences; a Liang envoy saw a Jin envoy in the lodge and reported that the Prince of Zhao had two minds.

value.zh: 是時，魏博羅紹威卒，梁因欲盡取河北，開平四年冬，遣供奉官杜廷隱監魏博將夏諲，以兵三千襲深、冀二州，以王景仁為北面行營招討使。
value.en: Luo Shaowei of Wei Bo had just died, and Liang aimed to swallow Hebei. In the winter of Kaiping 4 Taizu sent Du Tingyin with Xia Yin and three thousand Wei Bo troops to strike Shen and Ji, and appointed Wang Jingren to command the northern front.
value.literal: At that time Luo Shaowei of Wei Bo had died; Liang wished to take all of Hebei. In the winter of Kaiping 4 he sent the palace attendant Du Tingyin to supervise the Wei Bo general Xia Yin with three thousand men in a surprise attack on Shen and Ji, and made Wang Jingren commander of the northern campaign.

value.zh: 镕懼，乞兵於晉。
value.en: Terrified, Rong begged Jin for aid.
value.literal: Rong was afraid and begged troops from Jin.

value.zh: 晉人擊敗景仁於柏鄉，梁遂失鎮、定，而莊宗由此益強，北破幽、燕，南並魏博，镕常以兵從。
value.en: Jin routed Jingren at Bocheng. Liang lost Zhen and Ding; Zhuangzong grew mighty—conquering You and Yan in the north, swallowing Wei Bo in the south—with Rong’s armies often at his side.
value.literal: Jin defeated Jingren at Bocheng; Liang then lost Zhen and Ding, and Zhuangzong grew stronger—north he broke You and Yan, south he absorbed Wei Bo, and Rong often marched with him.

value.zh: 镕德晉甚。
value.en: Rong owed Jin a deep debt of gratitude.
value.literal: Rong was deeply grateful to Jin.

value.zh: 明年，會莊宗於承天軍，奉觴為壽，莊宗以镕父友，尊禮之，酒酣為镕歌，拔佩刀斷衣而盟，許以女妻镕子昭誨。
value.en: The next year he met Zhuangzong at Chengtian Army and toasted his health. Zhuangzong, who had known Rong’s father, treated him with ceremony. Drunk, he sang for Rong, drew his blade, cut his own robe for a blood oath, and pledged his daughter to Rong’s son Zhaohui.
value.literal: The next year he met Zhuangzong at Chengtian Army, raised a cup for his long life; Zhuangzong, treating him as his father’s friend, honored him. When the wine was deep he sang for Rong, drew his saber, cut his robe, and swore brotherhood, promising his daughter to Rong’s son Zhaohui.

value.zh: 镕為人仁而不武，未嘗敢為兵先，佗兵攻趙，常藉鄰兵為救。
value.en: Rong was gentle and no soldier; he never led from the front. Whenever Zhao was attacked he called on neighboring armies to save him.
value.literal: Rong was benevolent and unwarlike; he never dared lead the van. When other armies attacked Zhao he always borrowed neighbors for rescue.

value.zh: 當是時，諸鎮相弊於戰爭，而趙獨安，樂王氏之無事，都人士女褒衣博帶，務誇侈為嬉遊。
value.en: While the other circuits bled one another dry, Zhao alone stayed quiet. In the capital, men and women dressed in flowing silks and turned luxury into pastime.
value.literal: While the circuits wore one another down in war, Zhao alone remained at peace; the capital’s gentry and women wore loose robes and broad sashes and made a sport of display.

value.zh: 镕尤驕於富貴，又好左道，煉丹藥，求長生，與道士王若訥留遊西山，登王母祠，使婦人維錦繡牽持而上。
value.en: Rong flaunted his riches and dabbled in occult arts, brewing elixirs in search of immortality. With the Daoist Wang Ruone he toured West Mountain, climbed the Queen Mother temple, and had women in embroidered silks haul him up by rope.
value.literal: Rong was proudest of his wealth; he also loved heterodox ways, refined elixirs, and sought long life. With the Daoist Wang Ruone he lingered on West Mountain, climbed the Queen Mother shrine, and had women in brocade hold the ropes to pull him up.

value.zh: 每出，逾月忘歸，任其政於宦者。
value.en: He would be gone for months at a time and leave the realm to his eunuchs.
value.literal: Each time he went out he forgot to return for more than a month and left government to the eunuchs.

value.zh: 宦者石希蒙與镕同臥起。
value.en: The eunuch Shi Ximeng slept and rose at his side.
value.literal: The eunuch Shi Ximeng shared his bed and his waking hours.

value.zh: 天祐十八年冬，镕自西山宿鶻營莊，將還府，希蒙止之。
value.en: In the winter of Tianyou 18 Rong stayed at Gull Camp Manor on the road back from West Mountain. When he tried to return to the yamen, Ximeng barred him.
value.literal: In the winter of the eighteenth year of Tianyou, Rong lodged at Gull Camp Manor on his way back from West Mountain; as he was about to return to headquarters, Ximeng stopped him.

value.zh: 宦者李弘規諫曰：「今晉王身自暴露以親矢石，而大王竭軍國之用為遊畋之資，開城空宮，逾月不返，使一失閉門不納從者，大王欲何歸乎？」
value.en: Li Honggui warned him: “The Prince of Jin fights in person under fire, while you spend the treasury on pleasure. You leave the walls unmanned and the palace empty for months. If they lock the gates and turn you away, where will you sleep?”
value.literal: The eunuch Li Honggui remonstrated: “Now the Prince of Jin exposes his own body to arrows and stones, while you drain the state for hunting. You leave the city gates open and the palace empty, gone for more than a month. If once they shut the gates and refuse your followers, where will you go?”

value.zh: 镕懼，促駕，希蒙固止之。
value.en: Rong grew afraid and ordered his carriage; Ximeng would not let him go.
value.literal: Rong was afraid and urged his carriage on; Ximeng firmly held him back.

value.zh: 弘規怒，遣親事軍將蘇漢衡率兵擐甲露刃於帳前曰：「軍士勞矣！
value.en: Honggui in fury sent Su Hanheng of the household guard with armored men and naked swords to the tent: “The troops are exhausted!
value.literal: Honggui in anger sent the personal-guard general Su Hanheng with troops in armor and bare blades before the tent, saying: “The soldiers are weary!

value.zh: 願從王歸。」
value.en: They want to escort you home."
value.literal: We wish to follow the prince home."

value.zh: 弘規繼而進曰：「惑王者希蒙也，請殺之以謝軍士！」
value.en: Honggui pressed on: “Ximeng is the one who led you astray—kill him and appease the men!”
value.literal: Honggui then advanced and said: “The one who has misled the prince is Ximeng—kill him to answer the soldiers!”

value.zh: 鎔不答，弘規呼鎔甲士斬希蒙首，擲於鎔前，鎔懼，遽歸。
value.en: Rong said nothing. Honggui ordered the guards to behead Ximeng and fling the head at Rong’s feet. Rong fled home in terror.
value.literal: Rong did not answer; Honggui called Rong’s guards to cut off Ximeng’s head and throw it before him. Rong was afraid and hurried home.

value.zh: 使其子昭祚與大將張文禮族弘規、漢衡，收其偏將下獄，窮究反狀，親軍皆懼。
value.en: He sent his son Zhaozuo and Zhang Wenli to wipe out Honggui’s and Hanheng’s kin, jailed their officers, and hunted the plot to its roots. The household guard trembled.
value.literal: He had his son Zhaozuo and the great general Zhang Wenli execute the families of Honggui and Hanheng, imprisoned their subordinate generals, and investigated the rebellion to the end; the personal guard were all afraid.

value.zh: 文禮誘以為亂，夜半，親軍千餘人逾垣而入，镕方與道士焚香受箓，軍士斬镕首，袖之而出，因縱火焚其宮室，遂滅王氏之族。
value.en: Wenli turned their fear into revolt. After midnight a thousand guards poured over the wall. Rong was receiving a Daoist talisman when they struck off his head, hid it in a sleeve, and torched the palace. The Wang line ended that night.
value.literal: Wenli incited them to mutiny. At midnight more than a thousand guards scaled the wall and entered; Rong was just burning incense with a Daoist to receive a talisman when the soldiers cut off his head, tucked it in a sleeve, and left, then set fire and burned the palace—thus the Wang clan was extinguished.

value.zh: 镕小子昭誨，年十歲，其軍士有德镕者，藏之穴中，亂定，髡其發，被以僧衣，遇湖南人李震，匿昭誨於茶籠中，載之湖南，依南嶽為浮圖，易名崇隱。
value.en: Rong’s son Zhaohui was ten. Men who remembered Rong’s kindness hid him in a pit; when order returned they tonsured him and clothed him as a novice. A Hunanese named Li Zhen hid him in a tea crate and took him south. On South Mountain he entered the clergy as Chongyin.
value.literal: Rong’s young son Zhaohui was ten. Soldiers who had owed Rong kindness hid him in a cave; when the turmoil ended they shaved his head and dressed him as a monk. He met a Hunan man named Li Zhen, who hid Zhaohui in a tea basket and carried him to Hunan; he became a monk on South Mountain under the name Chongyin.

value.zh: 明宗時，昭誨已長，思歸，而镕故將符習為宣武軍節度使，震以歸習，習表於朝。
value.en: Under Mingzong, Zhaohui was grown and longed for home. Fu Xi, once Rong’s officer, now commanded Xuanwu. Li Zhen delivered the boy to him, and Fu Xi reported to court.
value.literal: In Mingzong’s time Zhaohui had grown and wished to return. Rong’s old general Fu Xi was military commissioner of Xuanwu; Zhen brought him to Xi, and Xi memorialized the court.

value.zh: 昭誨自稱前成德軍中軍使以見，拜考功郎中、司農少卿。
value.en: Zhaohui appeared as Chengde’s former central-army commander and received office as Reviewing Affairs cadre and Vice Minister of Agriculture.
value.literal: Zhaohui presented himself as former central-army commander of Chengde, was made Reviewing Affairs Cadre and Vice Minister of Agriculture.

value.zh: 周顯德中，猶為少府監云。
value.en: As late as Zhou Xiande he still held the post of Vice Director of Palace Manufactories.
value.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou he was still Vice Director of the Palace Workshops.

value.zh: 張文禮者，狡獪人也，镕惑愛之，以為子，號王德明。
value.en: Zhang Wenli was cunning. Rong doted on him, adopted him, and gave him the name Wang Deming.
value.literal: Zhang Wenli was a crafty man; Rong favored him, adopted him as a son, and styled him Wang Deming.

value.zh: 镕已死，文禮自為留後。
value.en: When Rong was dead Wenli declared himself acting commissioner.
value.literal: After Rong died Wenli made himself acting commissioner.

value.zh: 莊宗初納之，後知其通於梁也，遣趙故將符習與閻寶擊之。
value.en: Zhuangzong confirmed him at first, then learned he was dealing with Liang and sent Fu Xi and Yan Bao, old officers of Zhao, to bring him down.
value.literal: Zhuangzong at first accepted him; later learning he was in league with Liang he sent the Zhao veterans Fu Xi and Yan Bao against him.

value.zh: 文禮家鬼夜哭，野河水變為血，游魚皆死，文禮懼，病疽卒。
value.en: Spirits wailed in Wenli’s hall at night; the river outside turned to blood and the fish died. Wenli took fright and died of an abscess.
value.literal: Ghosts wept in Wenli’s house by night; the wild river ran blood; fish in the stream died; Wenli was afraid and died of a carbuncle.

value.zh: 子處瑾秘喪拒守，擊敗習等。
value.en: His son Chujin hid the corpse and held the city; he beat back Fu Xi’s force.
value.literal: His son Chujin concealed the death and held out; he defeated Fu Xi and the others.

value.zh: 以李嗣昭代之，嗣昭中流矢卒，以李存進代之，存進輒復戰歿，乃以符存審為招討使，遂破之。
value.en: Li Sizhao was sent to succeed him and died of an arrow wound. Li Cunjin followed and fell in the same fighting. At last Fu Cunshen took command and broke the holdout.
value.literal: Li Sizhao was sent to replace him; Sizhao took an arrow and died. Li Cunjin was sent in his place and immediately fell in battle again. Then Fu Cunshen was made campaign commander and at last broke them.

value.zh: 執文禮妻及子處瑾、處球、處琪等，折足歸於晉。
value.en: They captured Wenli’s wife and his sons Chujin, Chuqiu, and Chuqi, shattered their legs, and sent them to Jin.
value.literal: They seized Wenli’s wife and his sons Chujin, Chuqiu, and Chuqi, broke their legs, and sent them to Jin.

value.zh: 趙人請而醢之，磔文禮屍於市。
value.en: The Zhao people begged leave to pickle them alive; Wenli’s body was torn apart in the marketplace.
value.literal: The people of Zhao asked permission and pickled them; Wenli’s corpse was dismembered in the market.

value.zh: 都為人狡佞多謀，處直以為節度副使。
value.en: Du was sly, flattering, and scheming. Chuzhi made him deputy commissioner.
value.literal: Du was crafty, fawning, and full of schemes; Chuzhi made him deputy military commissioner.

value.zh: 張文禮弒王镕，莊宗發兵討文禮，處直與左右謀曰：「鎮，定之蔽也，文禮雖有罪，然鎮亡定不獨存。」
value.en: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong, and Zhuangzong marched to punish him. Chuzhi told his intimates: “Zhen and Ding are one shield. Wenli may be guilty, but if Zhen falls, Ding cannot stand alone.”
value.literal: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong; Zhuangzong raised troops to punish Wenli. Chuzhi consulted his close advisers, saying: “Zhen and Ding shield each other; though Wenli is guilty, if Zhen perishes Ding cannot stand alone.”

value.zh: 乃遣人請莊宗毋發兵，莊宗取所獲文禮與梁蠟書示處直曰：「文禮負我，師不可止。」
value.en: He sent envoys begging Zhuangzong to stay his hand. Zhuangzong showed him the wax-sealed letters Wenli had sent Liang: “Wenli has betrayed me. The campaign does not stop.”
value.literal: He sent men to ask Zhuangzong not to march; Zhuangzong took the captured letters between Wenli and Liang sealed in wax and showed Chuzhi, saying: “Wenli has betrayed me—the army cannot stop.”

value.zh: 處直有孽子郁，當郜之亡於晉也，郁亦奔焉，晉王以女妻之，為新州防禦使。
value.en: Chuzhi had a bastard son, Yu. When Gao fell to Jin, Yu fled there as well; the Prince of Jin gave him a princess and made him defender of Xinzhou.
value.literal: Chuzhi had a bastard son Yu; when Gao was lost to Jin, Yu had fled there too; the Prince of Jin gave him a daughter in marriage and made him defender of Xinzhou.

value.zh: 處直見莊宗必討文禮，益自疑，乃陰與郁交通，使郁北招契丹入塞以牽晉兵，且許召郁為嗣，都聞之不說。
value.en: Seeing Zhuangzong would not relent, Chuzhi grew afraid and wrote secretly to Yu, telling him to bring the Khitan across the border to pin Jin’s armies, and promised to name him heir. Du was not pleased.
value.literal: Seeing that Zhuangzong would surely punish Wenli, Chuzhi grew all the more suspicious and secretly communicated with Yu, having Yu summon the Khitan north of the passes to raid and tie down Jin’s troops; he also promised to call Yu back as heir. When Du heard it he was displeased.

value.zh: 而定人皆言契丹不可召，恐自貽患，處直不聽。
value.en: Everyone in Ding said the same: do not call the Khitan, or you invite ruin. Chuzhi would not hear it.
value.literal: Yet the people of Ding all said the Khitan must not be summoned, lest they bring disaster on themselves—Chuzhi would not listen.

value.zh: 郁自奔晉，常恐處直不容，因此大喜，以為乘其隙可取之，乃以厚賂誘契丹阿保機。
value.en: Yu had fled to Jin and always feared Chuzhi would never forgive him. Now he rejoiced, thinking the moment ripe to take Ding, and bribed Abaoji of the Khitan with heavy gifts.
value.literal: Yu, having fled to Jin, always feared Chuzhi would not spare him; he therefore rejoiced greatly, thinking that in this gap he could seize the circuit; he used rich bribes to entice the Khitan Abaoji.

value.zh: 阿保機舉國入寇，定人皆不欲契丹之舉，小吏和昭訓勸都舉事，都因執處直，囚之西宅，自為留後，凡王氏子孫及處直將校殺戮殆盡。
value.en: Abaoji invaded with the whole Khitan nation. Ding wanted no part of it. A clerk named He Zhaoxun urged Du to strike. Du seized Chuzhi, locked him in the west hall, declared himself acting commissioner, and butchered nearly every Wang and every loyal officer.
value.literal: Abaoji led his whole nation in invasion; the people of Ding all did not want the Khitan’s action. The petty clerk He Zhaoxun urged Du to act; Du therefore seized Chuzhi, imprisoned him in the western residence, and made himself acting commissioner, slaughtering nearly all the Wang clan and Chuzhi’s officers.

value.zh: 明年正月朔旦，都拜處直於西宅，處直奮起揕其胸而呼曰：「逆賊！
value.en: On New Year’s morning Du made Chuzhi bow to him in the west hall. Chuzhi lunged up and drove at his chest, shouting, “Traitor!
value.literal: On the first day of the first month of the next year Du had Chuzhi bow to him in the western residence; Chuzhi roused himself and stabbed at his chest, crying: “Rebel!

value.zh: 吾何負爾？」
value.en: What wrong did I ever do you?”
value.literal: What have I done to wrong you?”

value.zh: 然左右無兵，遂欲嚙其鼻，都掣袖而走，處直遂見殺。
value.en: He had no weapon but his teeth and tried to tear Du’s nose off. Du wrenched free and ran. They killed Chuzhi where he stood.
value.literal: But those at hand had no weapons; he then tried to bite off Du’s nose; Du pulled his sleeve free and fled—Chuzhi was thereupon killed.

value.zh: 守光素庸愚，由此益驕，為鐵籠、鐵刷，人有過者，坐之籠中，外燎以火，或刷剔其皮膚以死，燕之士逃禍於佗境。
value.en: Shouguang had never been bright; victory only swelled his pride. He built iron cages and iron brushes—offenders were locked in the cage while fire was lit outside, or their skin was scraped away until they died. The gentry of Yan fled across the borders to escape him.
value.literal: Shouguang had always been dull and foolish; from this he grew still more arrogant. He made iron cages and iron brushes; when anyone faulted, he seated them in the cage and burned fire outside, or scraped the skin from their bodies until they died. Men of Yan fled to other lands to escape disaster.

value.zh: 守光身衣赭黃，謂其將吏曰：「我衣此而南面，可以帝天下乎？」
value.en: Shouguang dressed himself in imperial ochre-yellow and asked his commanders: “Clothed like this and facing south, could I not rule the realm?”
value.literal: Shouguang himself wore ochre-yellow robes and said to his officers: “If I wear this and face south, can I be emperor of all under Heaven?”

value.zh: 孫鶴切諫以為不可。
value.en: Sun He pleaded with him to abandon the thought.
value.literal: Sun He urgently remonstrated that it could not be done.

value.zh: 梁攻趙，趙王王镕求救於守光，孫鶴曰：「今趙無罪，而梁伐之，諸侯救趙之兵，先至者霸，臣恐燕軍未出，而晉已先破梁矣，此不可失之時也。」
value.en: When Liang struck Zhao, Wang Rong of Zhao begged Shouguang for aid. Sun He said: “Zhao has done no wrong, yet Liang invades. Among the warlords, the first to rescue her will take the lead. I fear Jin will break Liang before our columns even march—this chance will not come again.”
value.literal: Liang attacked Zhao. Zhao king Wang Rong begged Shouguang for rescue. Sun He said: “Now Zhao is without guilt, yet Liang attacks her. Among the lords, whoever reaches Zhao first to save her will hold the hegemony. I fear before Yan’s army goes out, Jin will already have broken Liang—this is a moment not to be lost.”

value.zh: 守光曰：「趙王嘗與我盟而背之，今急乃來歸我；
value.en: Shouguang replied: “Wang Rong swore alliance with me and broke it; only now, desperate, does he crawl back.
value.literal: Shouguang said: “The Zhao king once allied with me and then turned his back; now in extremity he comes to submit to me;

value.zh: 且兩虎方鬥，可待之，吾當為卞莊子也。」
value.en: Besides, two tigers are already at each other’s throats. Let them fight. I mean to play Bian Zhuangzi.”
value.literal: Besides, two tigers are just now fighting—we may wait. I shall play Bian Zhuangzi.”

value.zh: 遂不出兵。
value.en: He sent no troops.
value.literal: So he did not send troops.

value.zh: 晉王果救趙，大敗梁兵於柏鄉，進掠邢、洺，至於黎陽。
value.en: Jin did rescue Zhao, crushing Liang at Boxiang, then raiding through Xing and Mo as far as Liyang.
value.literal: The Prince of Jin indeed rescued Zhao, greatly defeated Liang at Boxiang, advanced to plunder Xing and Mo, and reached Liyang.

value.zh: 守光聞晉空國深入梁，乃治兵戒嚴，遣人以語動鎮、定曰：「燕有精兵三十萬，率二鎮以從晉，然誰當主此盟者？」
value.en: Learning that Jin had stripped its home garrisons and plunged deep into Liang, Shouguang mustered his army, tightened discipline, and sent envoys to Zhen and Ding: “Yan can field thirty thousand picked men. I will march with your two circuits in Jin’s wake—but who leads this alliance?”
value.literal: Shouguang heard Jin had emptied its state and penetrated deep into Liang; then he drilled troops and set strict guard, and sent someone with words to move Zhen and Ding: “Yan has thirty thousand elite troops. I shall lead the two circuits to follow Jin—yet who shall head this alliance?”

value.zh: 晉人患之，謀曰：「昔夫差爭黃池之會，而越入吳；
value.en: Jin was alarmed. Its officers said: “Long ago Fuchai raced for precedence at Huangchi—and Yue walked into Wu.
value.literal: The Jin men were troubled. They consulted: “In ancient times Fuchai contested the meeting at Huangchi and Yue entered Wu;

value.zh: 項羽貪伐齊之利，而漢敗楚。
value.en: Xiang Yu chased profit against Qi, and Han broke Chu.
value.literal: Xiang Yu grasped at gain in attacking Qi and Han defeated Chu.

value.zh: 今吾越千里以伐人，而強燕在其後，此腹心之患也。」
value.en: We are a thousand li from home, fighting far afield, with powerful Yan at our back—that is a knife at the heart.”
value.literal: Now we march a thousand li to attack another while strong Yan is at our rear—this is a calamity in the belly and heart.”

value.zh: 乃為之班師。
value.en: For his sake they turned back.
value.literal: Thereupon they withdrew the army for him.

value.zh: 守光益以為諸鎮畏其強，乃諷諸鎮共推尊己，於是晉王率天德宋瑤、振武周德威、昭義李嗣昭、義武王處直、成德王镕等，以墨制冊尊守光為尚書令、尚父。
value.en: Shouguang took this as proof that every circuit feared him and began pressing them to elevate him together. The Prince of Jin then had Song Yao of Tiande, Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu, Wang Rong of Chengde, and others issue ink edicts naming Shouguang Director-in-Chief and Imperial Father.
value.literal: Shouguang thought still more that the circuits feared his strength; he hinted that the circuits jointly exalt him. Thereupon the Prince of Jin led Song Yao of Tiande, Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu, Wang Rong of Chengde, and others, with ink edicts enfeoffing Shouguang as Director-in-Chief and Imperial Father.

value.zh: 守光又遣告於梁，請授己河北兵馬都統，以討鎮、定、河東。
value.en: Shouguang also petitioned Liang to make him overall commander of Hebei armies and cavalry, with orders to strike Zhen, Ding, and Hedong.
value.literal: Shouguang also sent word to Liang, asking to be appointed commander-in-chief of Hebei military and horse, to attack Zhen, Ding, and Hedong.

value.zh: 梁遣閣門使王瞳拜守光河北采訪使。
value.en: Liang sent palace gate commissioner Wang Tong to invest him Hebei outreach commissioner.
value.literal: Liang sent Palace Gate Commissioner Wang Tong to invest Shouguang as Hebei outreach commissioner.

value.zh: 有司白守光，尚父受冊，用唐冊太尉禮儀，守光問曰：「此儀註何不郊天改元？」
value.en: The clerks told Shouguang that an Imperial Father’s investiture followed Tang’s rites for enfeoffing a Grand Marshal. Shouguang demanded: “Why does the manual say nothing about sacrificing to Heaven or changing the era name?”
value.literal: The office reported to Shouguang: receiving investiture as Imperial Father uses Tang ritual for investing the Grand Marshal. Shouguang asked: “Why does this ceremonial note not include sacrificing to Heaven and changing the reign title?”

value.zh: 有司曰：「此天子之禮也，尚父雖尊，乃人臣耳。」
value.en: They answered: “Those are the Son of Heaven’s rites. However honored the Imperial Father may be, he remains a subject.”
value.literal: The office said: “That is the Son of Heaven’s ritual; though the Imperial Father is exalted, he is still a subject.”

value.zh: 守光怒曰：「我為尚父，誰當帝者乎？
value.en: Shouguang flared: “I am Imperial Father—who then is emperor?
value.literal: Shouguang raged: “I am Imperial Father—who would be emperor?

value.zh: 且今天下四分五裂，大者稱帝，小者稱王，我以二千里之燕，獨不能帝一方乎？」
value.en: The realm is broken four and five ways; the mighty take the title of emperor, the lesser the title of king. With two thousand li of Yan, why should I alone not reign over my quarter?”
value.literal: Besides, today the realm is split four and five ways; the great call themselves emperors, the small call themselves kings. With my Yan of two thousand li, can I alone not be emperor of one quarter?”

value.zh: 乃械梁、晉使者下獄，置斧鑕於其庭，令曰：「敢諫者死！」
value.en: He had Liang and Jin envoys shackled and thrown into prison, set an axe and execution block in the courtyard, and announced: “Whoever advises against this dies!”
value.literal: Thereupon he fettered Liang and Jin envoys and cast them into prison, set axe and block in his courtyard, and proclaimed: “Whoever dares remonstrate dies!”

value.zh: 孫鶴進曰：「滄州之敗，臣蒙王不殺之恩，今日之事，不敢不諫。」
value.en: Sun He stepped forward: “After Cangzhou fell you spared my life. For what you mean to do today I cannot stay silent.”
value.literal: Sun He advanced and said: “At the defeat at Cangzhou I received the king’s grace of not being killed; for today’s affair I dare not fail to remonstrate.”

value.zh: 守光怒，推之伏鑕，令軍士割而啖之。
value.en: Shouguang had him thrown to the block and ordered the troops to carve off his flesh and eat it.
value.literal: Shouguang raged, pushed him down by the block, and ordered the soldiers to cut off pieces and devour him.

value.zh: 鶴呼曰：「不出百日，大兵當至！」
value.en: Sun He shouted: “In less than a hundred days a great army will come!”
value.literal: He cried: “Within a hundred days great troops will arrive!”

value.zh: 命窒其口而醢之。
value.en: They stuffed his mouth and pickled what remained of him.
value.literal: He was ordered silenced by stuffing his mouth, then minced.

value.zh: 守光遂以梁乾化元年八月自號大燕皇帝，改元曰應天，以王瞳、齊涉為左右相。
value.en: In the eighth month of Liang Qianhua 1 Shouguang proclaimed himself emperor of Great Yan, declared the era Yingtian, and made Wang Tong and Qi She his left and right chancellors.
value.literal: Shouguang then in the eighth month of Liang Qianhua year 1 styled himself Great Yan Emperor, changed the era title to Yingtian, and made Wang Tong and Qi She left and right chancellors.

value.zh: 晉遣太原少尹李承勛賀冊尚父，至燕，而守光已僭號。
value.en: Jin dispatched Li Chengxun, vice governor of Taiyuan, to congratulate the Imperial Father’s investiture; by the time he reached Yan, Shouguang had already seized the throne.
value.literal: Jin sent Taiyuan Vice Governor Li Chengxun to congratulate the investiture as Imperial Father; when he reached Yan, Shouguang had already usurped the throne.

value.zh: 有司迫承勛稱臣，承勛不屈，以列國交聘禮入見，守光怒，殺之。
value.en: The court forced Chengxun to declare himself a subject. He refused and entered audience by the protocol due a foreign envoy. Shouguang had him killed.
value.literal: The office pressed Chengxun to call himself subject; he would not bend, entered audience with ritual as between states on embassies. Shouguang raged and killed him.

value.zh: 守光與其妻李氏、祝氏，子繼珣、繼方、繼祚等，南走滄州，迷失道，至燕樂界中，數日不得食，遣其妻祝氏乞食於田家，田家怪而詰之，祝氏以實告，乃被擒送幽州。
value.en: Shouguang fled south toward Cangzhou with Lady Li, Lady Zhu, and his sons Jixun, Jifang, and Jizuo. They lost the road and wandered the borderlands of Yan and Le, days without food. He sent Lady Zhu to beg at a farmhouse; the farmers questioned her, she confessed, and they were seized and sent to Youzhou.
value.literal: Shouguang with his wife Lady Li, Lady Zhu, sons Jixun, Jifang, Jizuo, fled south toward Cangzhou, lost the road, reached the border of Yan and Le, several days without food. He sent his wife Lady Zhu to beg food from a farm household; the family found it strange and questioned her; she told the truth—they were seized and sent to Youzhou.

value.zh: 晉王方大饗軍，客將引守光見，晉王戲之曰：「主人何避客之遽也？」
value.en: The Prince of Jin was feasting the troops when Shouguang was brought in. He mocked him: “Why does the host flee his guest so fast?”
value.literal: The Prince of Jin was feasting the army. The client-officer led Shouguang in to audience. The Prince jested: “How quickly the host avoids his guest!”

value.zh: 守光叩頭請死，命械守光並其父仁恭以從軍。
value.en: Shouguang kowtowed and begged for death. The Prince had him shackled to his father Rengong and marched them with the army.
value.literal: Shouguang kowtowed begging death. He ordered Shouguang fettered together with his father Rengong to follow the army.

value.zh: 軍還過趙，趙王王镕會晉王，置酒，酒酣請曰：「願見仁恭父子。」
value.en: On the march home through Zhao, Wang Rong entertained the Prince of Jin. When the cups were warm he asked: “Let me see Rengong and his son.”
value.literal: The army returned passing through Zhao. Zhao king Wang Rong met the Prince of Jin and set out wine. When the wine was heated he requested: “I would see father and son Rengong.”

value.zh: 晉王命破械出之，引置下坐。
value.en: The Prince had their bonds removed and them brought out to sit below the dais.
value.literal: The Prince ordered their fetters broken and them brought out, seated below him.

value.zh: 飲食自若，皆無慚色。
value.en: They ate and drank as if nothing had happened, without a trace of shame.
value.literal: They ate and drank as usual, all without shame.

value.zh: 自晉兵出山東，已破孟遷，取邢、洺、磁三州，景福元年，乃大舉擊趙，下臨城。
value.en: Once Jin marched out of Shandong it had already broken Meng Qian and taken Xing, Ming, and Ci. In Jingfu 1 it struck Zhao in force and took Lincheng.
value.literal: When Jin armies marched out from Shandong they had already broken Meng Qian and taken Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures. In Jingfu 1 they launched a major assault on Zhao and took Lincheng.

value.zh: 鎔求救於李匡威，匡威來救，晉軍解去。
value.en: Rong called on Li Kuangwei; Kuangwei marched to save him and Jin pulled back.
value.literal: Rong begged Li Kuangwei for rescue; Kuangwei came and Jin withdrew.

value.zh: 明年，晉會王處存攻鎔堅固、新市。
value.en: The next year Jin and Wang Chucun attacked Jangu and Xinshi.
value.literal: The next year Jin joined Wang Chucun to attack Jangu and Xinshi.

value.zh: 晉王與處存皆自將，而鎔未嘗臨軍，遣追風都團練使段亮、翦寇都團練使馬珂等，以兵屬匡威而已。
value.en: Both commanders led in person, but Rong never took the field—he sent Duan Liang of Pursuing Wind and Ma Ke of Shearing Bandits and left the troops to Kuangwei.
value.literal: The Prince of Jin and Chucun both commanded in person, but Rong never went to the field himself—he sent Duan Liang, regimental training commissioner of Pursuing Wind, Ma Ke, regimental training commissioner of Shearing Bandits, and others, placing the troops under Kuangwei only.

value.zh: 匡威戰磁河，晉軍大敗。
value.en: At Ci River Kuangwei smashed the Jin army.
value.literal: Kuangwei fought at Ci River and Jin was badly defeated.

value.zh: 明年春，晉攻天長軍，鎔出兵救之，敗于叱日嶺，晉軍遂出井陘。
value.en: Next spring Jin attacked Tianchang Garrison. Rong sent relief, was beaten at Chiri Ridge, and Jin marched out through Jingxing Pass.
value.literal: The next spring Jin attacked Tianchang Garrison. Rong sent troops to relieve it, was beaten at Chiri Ridge, and Jin marched out through Jingxing Pass.

value.zh: 鎔又求救於匡威，晉軍解去。
value.en: Rong begged Kuangwei again and Jin withdrew once more.
value.literal: Rong again begged Kuangwei and Jin withdrew.

value.zh: 光化三年，梁兵攻定州，郜遣處直率兵拒之，戰于沙河，為梁兵所敗。
value.en: In Guanghua 3 Liang attacked Dingzhou. Gao sent Chuzhi to meet them at Shahe and was defeated.
value.literal: In Guanghua 3 Liang attacked Dingzhou; Gao sent Chuzhi to resist with troops. They fought at Shahe and were beaten by Liang.

value.zh: 兵返入城逐郜，郜出奔晉，亂兵推處直為留後。
value.en: The troops turned on Gao in the city; he fled to Jin and the mutineers made Chuzhi acting commissioner.
value.literal: Troops returning to the city drove out Gao; Gao fled to Jin and the mutineers made Chuzhi acting commissioner.

value.zh: 梁兵圍之，處直遣人告梁，請絕晉而事梁，出絹十萬匹犒軍，乃與梁盟。
value.en: Liang besieged him. Chuzhi offered to abandon Jin for Liang, sent a hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, and made peace with Liang.
value.literal: Liang besieged the city; Chuzhi sent word to Liang, offering to break with Jin and serve Liang, presented a hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, and made alliance with Liang.

value.zh: 梁太祖表處直義武軍節度使，累封太原王。
value.en: Taizu confirmed Chuzhi as Yiwu commissioner and repeatedly enfeoffed him Prince of Taiyuan.
value.literal: Liang Taizu memorialized Chuzhi as military commissioner of the Yiwu army and repeatedly enfeoffed him Prince of Taiyuan.

value.zh: 太祖即位，封處直北平王。
value.en: When Taizu took the throne he made Chuzhi Prince of Beiping.
value.literal: When Taizu took the throne he enfeoffed Chuzhi Prince of Beiping.

value.zh: 其後梁兵攻王鎔，鎔求救于晉，處直亦遣人至晉，願絕梁以自効。
value.en: Later, when Liang attacked Wang Rong and Rong called on Jin, Chuzhi also sent envoys offering to break with Liang and prove his loyalty.
value.literal: Later when Liang attacked Wang Rong and Rong begged Jin for aid, Chuzhi too sent envoys to Jin offering to break with Liang and prove his worth.

value.zh: 晉兵救鎔，處直以兵五千從，破梁軍於柏鄉。
value.en: Jin marched to save Rong; Chuzhi brought five thousand men and helped break Liang at Baixiang.
value.literal: Jin marched to save Rong; Chuzhi followed with five thousand men and defeated Liang at Baixiang.

value.zh: 其後晉北破燕，南取魏博，與梁戰河上，十餘年，處直未嘗不以兵從。
value.en: For more than ten years Jin broke Yan in the north, seized Weibo in the south, and fought Liang along the river; Chuzhi always marched with them.
value.literal: Thereafter Jin broke Yan in the north and took Weibo in the south and fought Liang along the Yellow River for more than ten years; Chuzhi never failed to follow with troops.

value.zh: 朱宣
value.en: Zhu Xuan
value.literal: Zhu Xuan

value.en: (Younger brother Jin appended)〉
value.literal: (Younger brother Jin appended)〉

value.zh: 鎮州張文禮殺王镕，使人告梁曰：「臣已北召契丹，願梁以兵萬人出德、棣州，則晉兵憊矣。」
value.en: Zhang Wenli of Zhen murdered Wang Rong and wrote Liang: “I have called Khitan from the north. Send ten thousand men from De and Di, and Jin will break.”
value.literal: Zhang Wenli of Zhen Prefecture killed Wang Rong and sent word to Liang: “Your servant has already summoned Khitan from the north; if Liang will march ten thousand men out of De and Di prefectures, the Jin army will be exhausted.”

value.zh: 敬翔以為然，巖與漢傑皆以為不可，乃止。
value.en: Jing Xiang agreed; Yan and Hanjie refused, and nothing was done.
value.literal: Jing Xiang thought it right, but Yan and Hanjie both said it could not be done, and so it stopped.

value.zh: 其後黜王彥章用段凝，皆巖力也。
value.en: Later the fall of Wang Yanzhang and the rise of Duan Ning were Yan’s work.
value.literal: Later the dismissal of Wang Yanzhang and the use of Duan Ning were both Yan’s doing.

value.zh: 晉數遣李存孝等出兵以窺山東，三州之人俘掠殆盡，赤地數千里，無復耕桑者累年。
value.en: Jin kept sending Li Cunxiao and others to probe Shandong. The three prefectures were stripped almost bare; for thousands of li nothing grew, and for years no one farmed or raised silkworms.
value.literal: Jin repeatedly sent Li Cunxiao and others to probe Shandong. The people of the three prefectures were plundered almost to extinction; for thousands of li the land was bare, and for years none farmed or raised silkworms again.

value.zh: 方立以孤城自守，求救于梁，梁方東事兗、鄆，不能救也。
value.en: Fangli held out in his lone city and begged Liang for help, but Liang was tied down in Yan and Yun and could not come.
value.literal: Fangli held his lone city and begged Liang for help, but Liang was then engaged in the east at Yan and Yun and could not save him.

value.zh: 文德元年，方立乞兵于王鎔以攻晉，鎔許之。
value.en: In Wende 1 Fangli asked Wang Rong for troops against Jin; Rong agreed.
value.literal: In the first year of Wende, Fangli asked Wang Rong for troops to attack Jin; Rong agreed.

value.zh: 方立乃遣其將奚忠信攻晉遼州，而鎔以佗故不能出兵。
value.en: Fangli sent Xi Zhongxin against Jin’s Liaozhou, but Rong could not march for other reasons.
value.literal: Fangli sent his general Xi Zhongxin to attack Jin’s Liaozhou, but Rong for other reasons could not march.

value.zh: 兵既失約，忠信大敗，而晉兵乘勝攻之。
value.en: When the promised troops never came, Zhongxin was smashed and Jin pressed the attack.
value.literal: When the promised troops failed to come, Zhongxin was utterly defeated, and Jin forces pressed the attack.

value.zh: 是時，梁將劉鄩等與莊宗相距澶、魏之間，兵數敗。
value.en: Liang generals led by Liu Zan were facing Zhuangzong between Cang and Wei, and their armies kept losing.
value.literal: At that time Liang generals Liu Zan and others faced Zhuangzong between Cang and Wei; their armies were repeatedly defeated.

value.zh: 巖曰：「古之王者必郊祀天地，陛下即位猶未郊天，議者以為朝廷無異藩鎮，如此何以威重天下？
value.en: Yan said: "Ancient kings always sacrificed to Heaven and Earth in the suburbs. Your Majesty has reigned yet never performed the suburban rite. People say the court looks no different from a frontier command—how will it awe the realm?
value.literal: Yan said: "Ancient kings invariably performed suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth. Your Majesty has been enthroned yet has still not sacrificed to Heaven. Critics say the court is no different from a frontier command—how can it awe the realm?

value.zh: 今河北雖失，天下幸安，願陛下力行之。」
value.en: Hebei is gone, but the rest of the empire is still at peace. I beg Your Majesty to do it at once."
value.literal: Hebei is lost, yet the rest of the empire is still at peace. I beg Your Majesty to do this resolutely."

value.zh: 敬翔以為不可，曰：「今府庫虛竭，箕斂供軍，若行郊禋，則必賞賚；
value.en: Jing Xiang refused: "The vaults are empty and every levy goes to the armies. Hold the suburban rites and you must shower rewards—
value.literal: Jing Xiang thought it impossible and said: "The treasury is empty and levies are scraped to feed the armies. If you perform the suburban rites, rewards must follow—

value.zh: 是取虛名而受實弊也。」
value.en: empty glory for real ruin."
value.literal: taking empty fame while suffering real harm."

value.zh: 末帝不聽，乃備法駕幸西京，而莊宗取楊劉，或傳：「晉兵入東都矣！」
value.en: The Last Emperor would not listen and prepared to go to the western capital. Zhuangzong took Yangliu. Rumors flew: "Jin is in the eastern capital!"
value.literal: The Last Emperor would not listen and prepared the imperial carriage for the western capital. Zhuangzong then took Yangliu. Some reported: "Jin troops have entered the eastern capital!"

value.zh: 或曰：「扼汜水矣！」
value.en: Others said: "They hold Sishui!"
value.literal: Others said: "They hold Sishui!"

value.zh: 或曰：「下鄆、濮矣！」
value.en: Or: "They have taken Yun and Pu!"
value.literal: Or: "They have taken Yun and Pu!"

value.zh: 京師大風拔木，末帝大懼，從官相顧而泣，末帝乃還東都，遂不果郊。
value.en: A gale uprooted trees in the capital. The Last Emperor panicked; courtiers wept at one another. He turned back to the eastern capital and never performed the suburban rite.
value.literal: A great wind in the capital uprooted trees. The Last Emperor was greatly afraid; attendants looked at one another and wept. He returned to the eastern capital and the suburban sacrifice was never carried out.

value.zh: 嗚呼，夷狄居處飲食，隨水草寒暑徙遷，有君長部號而無世族、文字記別，至於弦弓毒矢，強弱相並，國地大小，興滅不常，是皆烏足以考述哉！
value.en: Alas—the barbarian peoples shift their camps with the seasons, grazing and drinking wherever grass and water lead them. They have chieftains and tribal names, but no hereditary clans or written records by which to distinguish lineages. Bent bows and poisoned arrows decide who annexes whom; realms wax and wane without pattern. None of this is fit matter for full historical treatment.
value.literal: Alas, the barbarian peoples in their dwellings and diet follow grass and water, moving with cold and heat; they have chieftains and tribal names but no hereditary clans or written records for distinction; as for bent bows and poisoned arrows, the strong and weak annex one another, states and territories large and small, rise and fall without constancy—all these are utterly insufficient grounds for historical narration!

value.zh: 惟其服叛去來，能為中國利害者，此不可以不知也。
value.en: What we cannot afford to ignore is when they submit or rebel, come or go, and thereby help or harm the Central States.
value.literal: Only their submission, rebellion, departure, and coming—those who can benefit or harm China—this one must not fail to know.

value.zh: 自古夷狄之於中國，有道未必服，無道未必不來，蓋自因其衰盛。
value.en: From antiquity, barbarian peoples have not submitted simply because the Central States upheld the Way, nor stayed away simply because they did not. Their conduct has always tracked our strength or weakness.
value.literal: From antiquity the barbarian peoples toward China: when there is the Way they do not necessarily submit; when there is no Way they do not necessarily stay away—this is generally according to China's decline or flourishing.

value.zh: 雖嘗置之治外，而羈縻制馭恩威之際，不可失也。
value.en: Even when they are treated as beyond ordinary administration, the moments of loose control—when favor and awe are applied—must never be neglected.
value.literal: Although they have sometimes been placed outside regular governance, in the intervals of loose control, restraint, favor, and awe one must not lose hold.

value.zh: 其得之未必為利，失之有足為患，可不慎哉！
value.en: Winning their allegiance is not always an advantage; losing it can become a grave danger. How could one be careless?
value.literal: Gaining them is not necessarily profit; losing them is sufficient to become a calamity—how can one not be cautious!

value.zh: 作《四夷附錄》。
value.en: Hence this "Appendix on the Four Barbarian Peoples."
value.literal: I compose the "Appendix on the Four Barbarians."

value.zh: 莊宗討張文禮，圍鎮州。
value.en: Zhuangzong campaigned against Zhang Wenli and besieged Zhenzhou.
value.literal: Zhuangzong campaigned against Zhang Wenli and besieged Zhenzhou.

value.zh: 定州王處直懼鎮且亡，晉兵必並擊己，遣其子郁說契丹，使入塞以牽晉兵。
value.en: Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou feared that once Zhen fell, Jin armies would turn on him. He sent his son Yu to urge the Khitan to raid the border and draw Jin forces away.
value.literal: Dingzhou's Wang Chuzhi feared Zhen would soon perish and Jin troops would jointly strike him; he sent his son Yu to persuade the Khitan to enter the passes and pull Jin troops away.

value.zh: 郁謂阿保機曰：「臣父處直使布愚款曰：故趙王王镕，王趙六世，鎮州金城湯池，金帛山積，燕姬趙女，羅綺盈廷。
value.en: Yu told Abaoji, "My father Chuzhi sends his humble pledge: the late King of Zhao, Wang Rong, held Zhao for six generations. Zhenzhou is a fortress of gold and boiling moats, with treasure heaped like mountains, Yan and Zhao beauties, and silks filling the halls.
value.literal: Yu said to Abaoji: "My father Chuzhi sends me to lay out a foolish sincerity, saying: the former King of Zhao Wang Rong ruled Zhao six generations; Zhenzhou is golden city and boiling moat, gold and silks piled like mountains, Yan maidens and Zhao women, gauze and silk filling the hall.

value.zh: 張文禮得之而為晉所攻，懼死不暇，故皆留以待皇帝。」
value.en: Zhang Wenli seized it all but is now besieged by Jin and too terrified for his life to keep it—everything waits for Your Majesty."
value.literal: Zhang Wenli obtained it and is attacked by Jin; fearing death he has no leisure—therefore all is left awaiting Your Majesty.

value.zh: 阿保機大喜。
value.en: Abaoji was delighted.
value.literal: Abaoji was greatly pleased.

value.zh: 其妻述律不肯，曰：「我有羊馬之富，西樓足以娛樂，今舍此而遠赴人之急，我聞晉兵強天下，且戰有勝敗，後悔何追？」
value.en: His wife Shulü objected: "We have flocks and herds in plenty, and the Western Tower is amusement enough. Why leave this and rush to another's crisis? I hear Jin armies are the strongest under heaven—and battles have winners and losers. What use is regret afterward?"
value.literal: His wife Shulü would not agree, saying: "I have the wealth of sheep and horses; the Western Tower suffices for pleasure—now to abandon this and go far to another's urgency; I hear Jin troops are strongest under heaven, and moreover in battle there is victory and defeat—what regret can be pursued afterward?

value.zh: 阿保機躍然曰：「張文禮有金玉百萬，留待皇后，可共取之。」
value.en: Abaoji sprang up and said, "Zhang Wenli has millions in gold and jade set aside for the Queen—you and I can take it together."
value.literal: Abaoji leaped up and said: "Zhang Wenli has a million in gold and jade left awaiting the Queen—you may take it together."

value.zh: 於是空國入寇。
value.en: He then led the whole nation on an invasion.
value.literal: Thereupon he emptied the state and entered to raid.

value.zh: 郁之召契丹也，定人皆以為後患不可召，而處直不聽。
value.en: When Yu summoned the Khitan, everyone in Dingzhou warned that this would bring future disaster, but Chuzhi would not listen.
value.literal: In Yu's summoning of the Khitan, the people of Ding all considered it a later calamity and that they must not be summoned, but Chuzhi would not listen.

value.zh: 郁已去，處直為其子都所廢。
value.en: After Yu departed, Chuzhi was overthrown by his son Du.
value.literal: After Yu had gone, Chuzhi was deposed by his son Du.

value.zh: 阿保機攻幽州不克，又攻涿州，陷之。
value.en: Abaoji failed to take Youzhou, then attacked Zhuozhou and captured it.
value.literal: Abaoji attacked Youzhou without taking it, then attacked Zhuozhou and captured it.

value.zh: 聞處直廢而都立，遂攻中山，渡沙河。
value.en: Learning that Chuzhi had been deposed and Du installed, he marched on Zhongshan and crossed the Sha River.
value.literal: Hearing Chuzhi was deposed and Du established, he then attacked Zhongshan and crossed the Sha River.

value.zh: 都告急於莊宗。
value.en: Du sent an urgent appeal to Zhuangzong.
value.literal: Du reported urgency to Zhuangzong.

value.zh: 莊宗自將鐵騎五千，遇契丹前鋒於新城，晉兵自桑林馳出，人馬精甲，光明燭日。
value.en: Zhuangzong led five thousand armored horsemen in person and met the Khitan vanguard at Xincheng. Jin troops burst from Sanglin—men and horses in gleaming armor, light blazing like the sun.
value.literal: Zhuangzong personally led five thousand iron cavalry, met the Khitan vanguard at Xincheng; Jin troops burst out from Sanglin, men and horses in fine armor, brightness illuminating the sun.

value.zh: 虜騎愕然，稍卻，晉軍乘之，虜遂散走，而沙河冰薄，虜皆陷沒。
value.en: The enemy cavalry recoiled in shock. Jin forces pressed the attack and the Khitan broke and fled—but the ice on the Sha was thin, and many drowned.
value.literal: The barbarian cavalry were startled and slightly retreated; Jin troops pressed them and the barbarians then scattered in flight; but the Sha River ice was thin and the barbarians all sank and drowned.

value.zh: 阿保機退保望都。
value.en: Abaoji fell back to Wangdu.
value.literal: Abaoji withdrew to hold Wangdu.

value.zh: 會天大雪，契丹人馬饑寒，多死，阿保機顧盧文進以手指天曰：「天未使我至此。」
value.en: Heavy snow fell; Khitan men and horses starved and froze, and many died. Abaoji turned to Lu Wenjin, pointed at the sky, and said, "Heaven has not yet willed that I come here."
value.literal: It happened that heaven sent great snow; Khitan men and horses were hungry and cold and many died; Abaoji turned to Lu Wenjin, pointing with his finger at heaven, saying: "Heaven has not yet brought me here.

value.zh: 乃引兵去。
value.en: He then withdrew his army.
value.literal: Thereupon he led his troops away.

value.zh: 莊宗躡其後，見其宿處，環稭在地，方隅整然，雖去而不亂，嘆曰：「虜法令嚴，蓋如此也！」
value.en: Zhuangzong followed and inspected their camp: straw laid in a ring, corners neat and square—orderly even after they had gone. He sighed, "Their discipline is strict indeed!"
value.literal: Zhuangzong followed on their heels, saw their camping place—straw arranged in a ring on the ground, corners square and orderly, though departed yet not disordered—and sighed: "Barbarian laws and orders are strict—probably just like this!"

value.zh: 布智兒
value.en: Buzhier
value.literal: Buzhier

value.zh: 純只海，散術臺氏。
value.en: Chunzhihai belonged to the Sanshutai clan.
value.literal: Chunzhihai was of the Sanshutai clan.

value.zh: 弱冠宿衛太祖帳下，從征西域諸國有功。
value.en: In his youth he served in Genghis Khan's guard and distinguished himself in campaigns across the Western Regions.
value.literal: In his youth he served in the Great Khan's guard tent and followed campaigns in the Western Regions with merit.

value.zh: 歲癸巳，太宗命佩金虎符，充益都行省軍民達魯花赤，從大帥太出破徐州，擒金帥國用安。
value.en: In 1233 Emperor Ögedei ordered him to wear the gold tiger tally as chief military governor of the Yidu Branch Secretariat. He followed Grand Marshal Tachu in the capture of Xuzhou and took the Jin commander Guo Yong'an prisoner.
value.literal: In the year guisi Emperor Taizong ordered him to wear the gold tiger tally and appointed him Chief Darughachi of the military and civilians of the Yidu Branch Secretariat; he followed Grand Marshal Tachu in breaking Xuzhou and captured the Jin commander Guo Yong'an.

value.zh: 丁酉，以益都為皇太子分土，遷京兆行省都達魯花赤。
value.en: In 1237, when Yidu became the crown prince's fief, he was transferred to chief military governor of the Jingzhao Branch Secretariat.
value.literal: In dingyou Yidu became the crown prince's fief; he was transferred to Chief Darughachi of the Jingzhao Branch Secretariat.

value.zh: 至懷，值大疫，士卒困憊，有旨以本部兵就鎮懷孟。
value.en: On reaching Huai he encountered a great epidemic that left his soldiers exhausted. An order directed his forces to garrison Huai and Meng.
value.literal: Arriving at Huai, he encountered a great epidemic; soldiers were exhausted and weary; an order directed his command to garrison at Huai and Meng.

value.zh: 未幾，代察罕總軍河南，尋復懷孟。
value.en: Before long he replaced Chahan as overall commander of the Henan army, then soon returned to Huai and Meng.
value.literal: Before long he replaced Chahan in overall command of the Henan army, and soon returned to Huai and Meng.

value.zh: 己亥，同僚王榮潛畜異志，欲殺純只海，伏甲縶之，斷其兩足跟，以帛緘純只海口，置佛祠中。
value.en: In 1239 his colleague Wang Rong secretly plotted rebellion and attempted to kill Chunzhihai. Wang set armed men to seize him, severed both his Achilles tendons, bound his mouth with cloth, and left him in a Buddhist shrine.
value.literal: In jihai his colleague Wang Rong secretly harbored rebellious intent and wished to kill Chunzhihai; he set armed men to seize him, cut both his heel tendons, bound Chunzhihai's mouth with cloth, and placed him in a Buddhist shrine.

value.zh: 純只海妻喜禮伯倫聞之，率其眾攻榮家，奪出之。
value.en: When Chunzhihai's wife Xilibolun learned of this, she led her followers in an assault on Wang Rong's house and rescued her husband.
value.literal: When Chunzhihai's wife Xilibolun heard of this she led her followers to attack Rong's house and rescued him.

value.zh: 純只海裹瘡從二子馳旁郡，請兵討榮，殺之。
value.en: Wrapping his wounds, Chunzhihai rode with his two sons to a neighboring prefecture to raise troops, then returned to kill Wang Rong.
value.literal: Chunzhihai wrapped his wounds and with his two sons galloped to a neighboring prefecture to request troops to punish Rong and killed him.

value.zh: 朝廷遣使以榮妻孥貲產賜純只海家，且盡驅懷民萬餘口郭外，將戮之。
value.en: The court sent envoys granting Wang Rong's wife, children, and property to Chunzhihai's family and ordered more than ten thousand residents of Huai driven outside the walls for execution.
value.literal: The court sent envoys to grant Wang Rong's wife, children, and property to Chunzhihai's family, and moreover drove more than ten thousand Huai residents outside the walls, intending to slaughter them.

value.zh: 純只海力爭曰：「為惡者止榮一人耳，其民何罪。
value.en: Chunzhihai argued forcefully: "Only Wang Rong committed evil. What crime have the common people committed?
value.literal: Chunzhihai argued forcefully, saying, "The one who did evil was only Rong alone; what crime have the people committed?

value.zh: 若果盡誅，徒守空城何為？
value.en: If they are all put to death, of what use is holding an empty city?
value.literal: If they are indeed all put to death, of what use is merely holding an empty city?

value.zh: 茍朝廷罪使者以不殺，吾請以身當之。」
value.en: If the court would punish the envoy for failing to carry out the slaughter, I ask to answer for it with my own life."
value.literal: If the court would punish the envoy for not killing them, I ask to answer for it with my own person."

value.zh: 使者還奏，帝是其言，民賴不死。
value.en: The envoy returned and reported to the Emperor, who approved his argument. The people were spared.
value.literal: The envoy returned to report; the Emperor approved his words and the people relied on this and did not die.

value.zh: 純只海給榮妻孥券，放為民，遂以其宅為官廨，秋毫無所取。
value.en: Chunzhihai issued certificates freeing Wang Rong's wife and children as commoners, converted their residence into the government office, and took nothing for himself.
value.literal: Chunzhihai issued certificates to Wang Rong's wife and children and released them as commoners; he then made their residence the government office and took not the slightest thing.

value.zh: 郡人德之。
value.en: The people of the prefecture revered him for this.
value.literal: The people of the prefecture were grateful to him.

value.zh: 既入覲，太宗以純只海先朝舊臣，功績昭著，賜第一區於和林，尋以疾卒。
value.en: After he presented himself at court, Emperor Ögedei, recognizing Chunzhihai as a veteran minister of the previous reign with illustrious service, granted him a first-ranked residence at Karakorum. He soon died of illness.
value.literal: After entering for audience, Emperor Taizong because Chunzhihai was an old minister of the previous reign with illustrious achievements granted him a first-ranked residence at Karakorum; soon he died of illness.

value.zh: 敕葬山陵之側。
value.en: An edict ordered him buried beside the imperial tombs.
value.literal: An edict ordered him buried beside the imperial tombs.

value.zh: 張柔，字德剛，易州定興人，世力農。
value.en: Zhang Rou, styled Degang, came from Dingxing in Yizhou. His family had farmed the land for generations.
value.literal: Zhang Rou, style name Degang, was a native of Dingxing in Yizhou; his family for generations labored as farmers.

value.zh: 柔少慷慨，尚氣節，善騎射，以豪俠稱。
value.en: As a young man Rou was open-handed and chivalrous, prized loyalty and courage, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and famed as a gallant free spirit.
value.literal: In his youth Rou was magnanimous, esteemed integrity and honor, excelled at mounted archery, and was known as a bold hero.

value.zh: 金貞祐間，河北盜起，柔聚族黨保西山東流寨，選壯士，結隊伍以自衛，盜不敢犯。
value.en: In the Jinyou reign of the Jin, brigands spread across Hebei. Rou rallied his kinsmen to defend Dongliu Stockade in the Western Hills, picked stalwart fighters, and organized armed bands for protection so that raiders dared not trouble them.
value.literal: During the Jinyou era of Jin, bandits rose in Hebei. Rou gathered his clan to hold Dongliu Stockade in the Western Hills, selected strong men, formed companies for self-defense, and bandits did not dare molest them.

value.zh: 郡人張信假柔聲勢，納流人女為妻，柔鞭信百而還其女。
value.en: A local man named Zhang Xin traded on Rou's reputation to seize a refugee woman as his wife. Rou had Xin whipped a hundred times and sent the woman back.
value.literal: A townsman Zhang Xin borrowed Rou's prestige, took a refugee woman as wife; Rou flogged Xin a hundred strokes and returned the woman.

value.zh: 信憾之，謀結黨害柔。
value.en: Xin nursed a grudge and schemed with allies to destroy Rou.
value.literal: Xin bore resentment and plotted with a faction to harm Rou.

value.zh: 未幾，信有罪當誅，柔救之得免，於是驍勇之士，多慕義從之。
value.en: Soon afterward Xin was condemned to death for a crime, but Rou intervened and he was pardoned. From then on many bold fighters were drawn to his sense of justice and joined his cause.
value.literal: Before long Xin committed a crime warranting execution; Rou saved him and he was spared, whereupon many fierce warriors admired his righteousness and followed him.

value.zh: 中都經略使苗道潤承製授柔定興令，累遷清州防禦使。
value.en: Miao Daorun, military commissioner of the Central Capital, appointed Rou magistrate of Dingxing by imperial order, and Rou rose through successive posts to Defender of Qingzhou.
value.literal: The Central Capital military commissioner Miao Daorun by imperial commission appointed Rou magistrate of Dingxing; he was promoted repeatedly to Defender of Qingzhou.

value.zh: 道潤表其才，加昭毅大將軍，遙領永定軍節度使，兼雄州管內觀察使，權元帥左都監，行元帥府事。
value.en: Daorun recommended his abilities to the throne. Rou was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor, given the nominal post of Military Commissioner of the Yongding Army, made concurrent Commissioner of Observation for Xiongzhou, named acting Left Overseer of the Marshalate, and entrusted with the affairs of the marshal's headquarters.
value.literal: Daorun memorialized his talent; he was made Grand General of Manifest Valor, remotely bore Military Commissioner of Yongding Army, concurrently Commissioner of Observation within Xiongzhou, Acting Left Overseer of the Marshalate, and administered the Marshal's headquarters.

value.zh: 繼而道潤為其副賈瑀所殺，瑀遣使以好辭來告曰：「吾得除道潤者，以君不助兵故也。」
value.en: Daorun was soon killed by his deputy Jia Yu, who sent an envoy with soothing words: "I was able to eliminate Daorun because you did not send troops to help him."
value.literal: Thereafter Daorun was killed by his deputy Jia Yu; Yu sent an envoy with conciliatory words saying: "I was able to remove Daorun because you did not aid his troops."

value.zh: 柔怒叱使者曰：「瑀殺吾所事，吾食瑀肉且未足快意，反以此言相戲耶！」
value.en: Rou thundered at the envoy: "Yu murdered the lord I served. I would not be satisfied even if I devoured his flesh—and you dare mock me with words like these!"
value.literal: Rou angrily rebuked the envoy: "Yu killed the man I served; I would not yet be satisfied even if I ate Yu's flesh, and yet you jest with such words!"

value.zh: 遂移檄道潤部曲，會易州軍市川，誓眾為之復仇，眾皆感泣。
value.en: He issued a call to arms to Daorun's troops, mustered them at Junshichuan in Yizhou, and led the host in swearing vengeance. The men wept as one.
value.literal: He then issued a proclamation to Daorun's troops, assembled them at Junshichuan in Yizhou, and swore the host to avenge him; all were moved to tears.

value.zh: 適道潤麾下何伯祥得道潤所佩金虎符以獻，因推柔行經略使事。
value.en: At that moment He Boxiang, a commander under Daorun, presented the golden tiger tally that Daorun had carried, and the troops pressed Rou to assume the duties of military commissioner.
value.literal: Just then He Boxiang of Daorun's command obtained and presented the golden tiger tally Daorun had worn, and on that basis they urged Rou to act as military commissioner.

value.zh: 事聞，加驃騎將軍、中都留守，兼大興府尹、本路經略使，行元帥事。
value.en: When word reached the court, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, made Garrison Commander of the Central Capital and concurrently Prefect of Daxing and military commissioner of the circuit, and entrusted with marshal's authority.
value.literal: When the matter was reported, he was made General of Agile Cavalry, Garrison Commander of the Central Capital, concurrently Prefect of Daxing and military commissioner of the circuit, and acted as marshal.

value.zh: 辛巳，金懷州元帥王榮、潞州元帥裴守謙、澤州太守王珍皆以城降。
value.en: On xinsi day the Jin commanders Wang Rong of Huaizhou, Pei Shouqian of Luzhou, and Wang Zhen, defender of Zezhou, all surrendered their cities.
value.literal: On the day xinsi the Jin commanders Wang Rong of Huaizhou, Pei Shouqian of Luzhou, and Defender Wang Zhen of Zezhou all surrendered their cities.

value.zh: 壬午，攻濟南水寨，破之。
value.en: On renwu day he attacked the Jinan river stockade and captured it.
value.literal: On the day renwu he attacked the Jinan river stockade and broke it.

value.zh: 癸未，徇山西，遂克三關，不浹旬，定四十餘寨。
value.en: On guiwei day he swept through Shanxi and took the Three Passes. In less than ten days he secured more than forty stockades.
value.literal: On the day guiwei he swept Shanxi, then took the Three Passes; in less than ten days he settled more than forty stockades.

value.zh: 兵至河衛，喜曰：「河衛者，夷門之限也。
value.en: When his army reached Hewei he rejoiced and said, "Hewei is the gateway to Yimen.
value.literal: When the army reached Hewei he rejoiced: "Hewei is the barrier of Yimen.

value.zh: 河衛既破，則夷門不能守矣。」
value.en: Once Hewei falls, Yimen cannot be held."
value.literal: Once Hewei is broken, Yimen cannot be held."

value.zh: 嚴實以兵來會，請自攻河衛，天倪曰：「合達、蒲瓦，亦勍敵也。」
value.en: Yan Shi arrived with troops to join him and asked to take Hewei himself. Tianni said, "Hedda and Puwa are formidable enemies as well."
value.literal: Yan Shi came with troops to join him and asked to attack Hewei himself; Tianni said: "Hedda and Puwa are also formidable foes."

value.zh: 實曰：「易與耳，保為公破之。」
value.en: Shi replied, "They will be easy. I guarantee I will break them for you."
value.literal: Shi said: "They are easy opponents—I guarantee to break them for you."

value.zh: 明日，實與蒲瓦兵遇於南門，合達兵自北奄至，實兵敗，竟為所執。
value.en: The next day Shi met Puwa's troops at the south gate. Hedda's forces swept down from the north. Shi's army was defeated and he was captured.
value.literal: The next day Shi met Puwa's troops at the south gate; Hedda's forces suddenly arrived from the north; Shi's army was defeated and he was finally captured.

value.zh: 天倪曰：「合達以實歸汴，必以今夕。」
value.en: Tianni said, "Hedda will escort Shi back to Bian. It must happen tonight."
value.literal: Tianni said: "Hedda will take Shi back to Bian—it must be tonight."

value.zh: 急命馮存、杜必貴率壯士一千三百，伏延津柳渡。
value.en: He urgently ordered Feng Cun and Du Bigui to lead thirteen hundred picked warriors in ambush at Yanjin Willow Ford.
value.literal: He urgently ordered Feng Cun and Du Bigui to lead thirteen hundred stalwart warriors to ambush at Yanjin Willow Ford.

value.zh: 果夜縛實過延津，遇存等，與戰，敗之，實得脫歸，必貴戰死。
value.en: That night the escort bound Shi and passed through Yanjin. They met Feng Cun's ambush, were defeated, and Shi escaped. Du Bigui died in the fighting.
value.literal: Indeed at night they bound Shi and passed Yanjin; they met Cun and others, fought, were defeated, Shi escaped and returned, and Bigui died in battle.

value.zh: 未幾，帝命天倪回軍真定。
value.en: Soon afterward the emperor ordered Tianni to return his army to Zhending.
value.literal: Before long the emperor ordered Tianni to return his army to Zhending.

value.zh: 甲申夏，大名總管彭義斌以宋兵犯河朔，天倪逆戰於恩州，義斌敗，入保大名。
value.en: In the summer of the jiashen year, Peng Yibin, prefect of Daming, invaded Heshuo with Song troops. Tianni met him at Enzhou, routed him, and drove him back into Daming.
value.literal: In summer of the year jiashen, Daming prefect Peng Yibin with Song troops invaded Heshuo; Tianni met them at Enzhou; Yibin was defeated and withdrew into Daming.

value.zh: 乙酉，師還，聞武仙之黨據西山腰水、鐵壁二寨以叛，天倪直搗其巢穴，盡掩殺之。
value.en: On yiyou day the army returned. Learning that Wu Xian's followers had rebelled and seized Yaoshui and Tiebi stockades in the Western Hills, Tianni struck their strongholds directly and slaughtered them to the last man.
value.literal: On the day yiyou the army returned; hearing that Wu Xian's partisans held Yaoshui and Tiebi stockades in the Western Hills in rebellion, Tianni struck straight at their nests and slaughtered them all.

value.zh: 仙怒，謀作亂，乃設宴邀天倪。
value.en: Wu Xian, enraged, plotted rebellion and invited Tianni to a banquet.
value.literal: Xian in anger plotted rebellion and set a banquet to invite Tianni.

value.zh: 有知其謀者，止天倪毋往，天倪不從，遂為仙所殺。
value.en: Someone who knew the plot warned Tianni not to go. He refused to listen and was killed by Wu Xian.
value.literal: Someone who knew the plot urged Tianni not to go; Tianni would not listen and was thereupon killed by Xian.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第032卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 32.
value.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 32.

value.zh: 初，紅陽侯立不得輔政，疑為長毀譖，常怨毒長；
value.en: Earlier, Marquis Li of Hongyang, denied a role in government, suspected Chang of slandering him and constantly hated him;
value.literal: Earlier, Marquis Li of Hongyang, not obtaining a role in government, suspected Chang of slandering him and constantly bore bitter hatred toward Chang;

value.zh: 上知之。
value.en: the emperor knew this.
value.literal: the emperor knew this.

value.zh: 及長當就國，立嗣子融從長請車騎，長以珍寶因融重遺立。
value.en: When Chang was about to depart for his fief, Li's heir Rong followed Chang to request chariots and escort; Chang sent a heavy gift of treasures to Li through Rong.
value.literal: When Chang was about to go to his state, Li's heir Rong followed Chang to request chariots and horsemen; Chang used treasures through Rong to send a heavy gift again to Li.

value.zh: 立因上封事，為長求留，曰：「陛下既托文以皇太后故，誠不可更有它計。」
value.en: Li thereupon submitted a sealed memorial seeking to retain Chang, saying, "Your Majesty has already committed in writing on account of the Empress Dowager—there truly must not be another plan."
value.literal: Li thereupon submitted a sealed memorial seeking to retain Chang, saying: "Your Majesty has already entrusted the matter to writing on account of the Empress Dowager—truly there must not be another plan."

value.zh: 於是天子疑焉，下有司按驗。
value.en: Thereupon the emperor grew suspicious and ordered the responsible offices to investigate.
value.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven grew suspicious and sent it down to the responsible offices for investigation and verification.

value.zh: 吏捕融，立令融自殺以滅口。
value.en: Officials arrested Rong; Li ordered Rong to kill himself to silence him.
value.literal: Officials arrested Rong; Li ordered Rong to kill himself to silence him.

value.zh: 上愈疑其有大奸，遂逮長系洛陽詔獄，窮治。
value.en: The emperor grew still more suspicious of great treachery and arrested Chang, imprisoning him in the Luoyang imperial prison for a full investigation.
value.literal: The emperor grew still more suspicious of great treachery and thereupon arrested Chang and imprisoned him in the Luoyang imperial prison, investigating to the end.

value.zh: 長具服戲侮長定宮，謀立左皇后，罪至大逆，死獄中。
value.en: Chang fully confessed to mocking Changding Palace and plotting to install a Left Empress—crime reaching great treason; he died in prison.
value.literal: Chang fully confessed to mocking Changding Palace and plotting to install a Left Empress—crime reaching great treason; he died in prison.

value.zh: 妻子當坐者徙合浦；
value.en: Wife and children who shared punishment were exiled to Hepu;
value.literal: Wife and children who should share punishment were exiled to Hepu;

value.zh: 母若歸故郡。
value.en: his mother Ru returned to her native commandery.
value.literal: his mother Ru returned to her native commandery.

value.zh: 上使廷尉孔光持節賜廢後藥，自殺。
value.en: The emperor sent Commandant of Justice Kong Guang with credentials to bestow poison on the deposed empress for suicide.
value.literal: The emperor sent Commandant of Justice Kong Guang with credentials to bestow poison on the deposed empress for self-destruction.

value.zh: 丞相方進復劾奏「紅陽侯立，狡猾不閫，請下獄。」
value.en: Chancellor Fangjin again impeached, saying, "Marquis Li of Hongyang is crafty and unbounded—please send him to prison."
value.literal: Chancellor Fangjin again impeached and memorialized: "Marquis Li of Hongyang is crafty and does not keep to bounds—please send him to prison."

value.zh: 上曰：「紅陽侯，朕之舅，不忍致法；
value.en: The emperor said, "Marquis Li of Hongyang is Our maternal uncle—we cannot bear to apply the law;
value.literal: The emperor said: "Marquis Li of Hongyang is Our maternal uncle—we cannot bear to apply the law;

value.zh: 遣就國。」
value.en: send him to his fief."
value.literal: send him to his state."

value.zh: 於是方進復奏立黨友後將軍朱博、巨鹿太守孫閎，皆免官，與故光祿大夫陳鹹皆歸故郡。
value.en: Thereupon Fangjin again memorialized that Li's associates Rear General Zhu Bo and Administrator of Julu Sun Hong were all removed from office, and together with former Grand Master of Splendor Chen Xian returned to their native commanderies.
value.literal: Thereupon Fangjin again memorialized that Li's partisan associates Rear General Zhu Bo and Administrator of Julu Sun Hong were all removed from office, and together with former Grand Master of Splendor Chen Xian all returned to their native commanderies.

value.zh: 鹹自知廢錮，以憂死。
value.en: Xian, knowing himself disgraced and barred from office, died from grief.
value.literal: Xian, knowing himself disgraced and barred, died from grief.
